text:
ari: quick heads-up — after the mixed precision kernel swap on canary (int8 + fp8 path) i see intermittent NaNs during decode when KV cache is enabled. started ~11:13 PDT on canary-2, ~12% tail latency spike and ~5% token dropouts :frowning:

jess: ugh. did you repro locally with the same batch profile? can you paste a minimal repro or the log snippet?

ari: repro is small. repro steps: set model=redwood-v2-12b-quant (int8 base, fp8 matmul), enable kv-cache, run a 2k token cold-start then repeated short queries. log: 
```
[2026-03-18 11:13:07] INFO decode: step=1245 token=5023 softmax=nan
[2026-03-18 11:13:07] WARN runtime: detected inf in attention scores, flushing KV
[2026-03-18 11:13:07] ERROR kernel_selector: selected int8-fp8-mix kernel v3.2
```

sam: interesting. i saw similar in profiling — the fp8 scale table on a few layers was ~1e-38 after calibration which is basically denorm. when we multiply by cached kv that has fp8->fp32 rescale we hit underflow -> unexpected NaN after softmax. profiler excerpt: 
```
layer 14: fp8_scale=1.2e-38  (quant zero bias ~ 128)
layer 15: fp8_scale=3.4e-02
latency per token (canary): 28.1ms vs baseline 25.1ms (+12%)
throughput (batched): 4.0 kTokens/s vs 5.0 kTokens/s (-20%)
```

luis: if scale is 1e-38 that's basically flush to zero on most hw. are we accidentally mixing calibration sets between short and long seq modes? maybe the calibration pass used a different seq-len distribution.

ari: exact suspicion. the calibration job we used was run with seq=512 samples, but production traffic has many short queries with kv reuse; scales don't generalize. noticed that the kernel selector prefers the int8-fp8-mix kernel when average seq len < 64 due to latency heuristics — but kv cache reuse path doesn't rescale cached tensors properly.

jess: two immediate mitigations: 1) force fallback to stable int8-only kernel for any request that reuses KV from a model version with incompatible calibration metadata; 2) clamp scales during calibration to a floor (eg min_scale=1e-6) and emit warning when many layers near floor. plan?

sam: quick patch i ran locally: 
```
# in kernel_selector
if kv_reuse and any(layer.scale < 1e-7):
    choose_kernel('int8-stable')
```
reproduced: NaNs disappeared, tail latency back to ~25.6ms. But throughput dropped for short batched lanes ~10% (expected).

benchbot: perf-run finished: canary-2 (patch) vs canary-1 (live) — median latency: 25.7ms vs 25.0ms, p95: 46ms vs 51ms, NaN errors: 0/10k vs 27/10k.

luis: good. long term we should: - add scale-compatibility tags to model artifacts (per-layer min/max, calibration-dist) - have kernel selector check compatibility / do on-the-fly recalibration for cached kv when cheap - upstream smoothquant-like rescale option at init to avoid tiny scales

jess: for rollout: push the simple kernel-fallback guard to canary (small perf regress in certain cases) + enforce calibration floor in quant pipeline. also add a CI check that runs a short kv-reuse scenario during quant calibration and fails if any layer scale < 1e-7.

ari: creating PR now for the fallback. will attach logs and the repro script. tagging @jess @sam for review. thanks all :thumbsup:
